### Summary

snapy is built on PyTorch and on three numerical packages from the same group: kintera (thermodynamics and
chemistry), pyharp (the time integrator) and pydisort (radiative transfer, linked but not called). On Linux it also
depends on commux, the communication layer of the UCX process group, and on pinc, which locates the parallel NetCDF
library. A reader who installs or changes snapy needs to know which of these are required, which versions the build
accepts, and where the build metadata leaves a requirement undeclared. This appendix lists them. The source pins of
this report are not version constraints, and the table keeps the two apart.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Kintera supplies thermodynamics and kinetics; pyharp supplies the time integrator.
Disort is a required C++ link dependency and Python import, even though the inspected compiled source has no
radiative-transfer solver call. Dependency availability does not imply active radiation coupling.
:::

| component | use in snapy | required version at the snapy pin |
|---|---|---|
| kintera | moist EOS, saturation adjustment, driver kinetics | at least 2.6.3 in CMake (`find_package(Kintera 2.6.3 REQUIRED)`) and in Python build and runtime metadata (`kintera>=2.6.3`) |
| pyharp / CMake Harp | integrator options, stage weights and stage combination | required by CMake; no version minimum or exact version specified |
| pydisort / CMake Disort | C++ shared-library link and Python package import | required by CMake; no version minimum or exact version specified |
| commux | process group over UCX (@sec-ch14-backends) | `commux>=0.1.4` on Linux in Python build and runtime metadata; CMake links `commux::commux` when UCX is found |
| pinc | locates the PnetCDF headers and library (@sec-ch14-pnetcdf) | `pinc>=0.2.0` on Linux in Python build and runtime metadata |

: Requirements, distinct from source pins and tested compatibility. {#tbl-appe-requirements}

`find_package` declares these CMake requirements: `Disort` and `Harp` with no version, `Kintera 2.6.3`
({{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}). `FindKintera` enforces the floor at configure time: it reads `kintera.__version__`
and fails with "snapy requires kintera >= 2.6.3 (…)" below it ({{< code cmake/modules/FindKintera.cmake >}}).
Python `[build-system] requires` and `[project] dependencies` both contain `kintera>=2.6.3`
({{< code pyproject.toml >}}).
Neither Python list declares pyharp or pydisort. They are required all the same, and the version a build accepts is
not bounded, in four steps:

1. *The Python package imports both.* `python/__init__.py` imports `pydisort`, `pyharp` and `kintera` before it loads
   the compiled extension, so `import snapy` fails without either ({{< code python/__init__.py >}}).
2. *The C++ library links both.* `src/CMakeLists.txt` lists `DISORT_LIBRARY`, `HARP_LIBRARY` and `KINTERA_LIBRARY`
   among the `PUBLIC` link libraries of the `snap` target ({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}), and the top-level
   `find_package(Disort REQUIRED)`, `find_package(Harp REQUIRED)` stop the configure without them.
3. *The locators read a version but are given none to compare.* `FindHarp` and `FindDisort` run
   `import pyharp; print(pyharp.__version__)` (likewise for pydisort) and stop if that fails. They pass the result as
   `VERSION_VAR`, but `find_package` is called without a version argument, so any found version is accepted
   ({{< code cmake/modules/FindHarp.cmake >}}, {{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake >}}).
4. *Hence* their absence from `pyproject.toml` is a packaging gap, not evidence that they are optional, and no
   compatible version range can be read from the metadata. The source pins of this report fix the API evidence; they
   are not version constraints.

### Derivation

This appendix inventories interfaces and dependencies; it introduces no numerical scheme or equation.
Thermodynamic, integration and moist-coupling derivations belong to the corresponding chapters.
A linked library, an imported Python package and a numerical call are separate facts and are recorded separately.

### Numerical method

Kintera's `ThermoYImpl` is constructed by the moist-mixture EOS. `compute` converts conserved internal energy to
temperature (`VU->T`) and temperature to pressure (`VT->P`); `specific_heat_cv` obtains mixture heat capacity.
On the final integrator stage, the mesh block calls `pthermo->forward` with density, internal energy density and
species mass fractions, then writes the adjusted fractions back. The pinned kintera `ThermoYImpl::forward`
accepts this contract ([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:275-284`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L275-L284)); it is separate from the example driver's kinetic update.
The driver refreshes primitives after dynamics, evaluates rates and their Jacobian, and calls `evolve_implicit`.

Pyharp is used through C++ `harp::Integrator`: snapy parses its options, creates the integrator and invokes
`pintg->forward` to combine both hydro and scalar stage increments. This is active solver use of pyharp,
independent of any external radiation functionality that package may provide.

Disort is explicitly in the `PUBLIC` libraries of the `snap` shared target, through `DISORT_LIBRARY`
({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}). `FindDisort` locates `disort_release` ({{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake >}}) and obtains version information
by importing pydisort ({{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake >}}). Harp similarly reads `pyharp.__version__`
({{< code cmake/modules/FindHarp.cmake >}}) and requires its headers/library ({{< code cmake/modules/FindHarp.cmake >}}).

### Code

**What to install.** For a CPU build on Linux: PyTorch 2.10.0, `kintera>=2.6.3`, pyharp, pydisort, and, for the UCX
process group and PnetCDF output, `commux>=0.1.4` and `pinc>=0.2.0`. The versions are those of the build metadata
above; for pyharp and pydisort none is declared.

```bash
python -m pip install "torch==2.10.0" "kintera>=2.6.3" pyharp pydisort "commux>=0.1.4" "pinc>=0.2.0"
```

These metadata requirements do not establish a tested compatible combination; use the preface recipe for a complete build.

**What the build refuses, and why.** In order, at configure time:

1. *An importable package is missing.* `FindKintera`, `FindHarp` and `FindDisort` each import their Python package
   to read its version, and stop with "cannot determine PEP 440 version of …" if the import fails. The C++ library
   is located from the Python package.
2. *kintera is older than 2.6.3.* `FindKintera` fails with "snapy requires kintera >= 2.6.3 (…), found …". The
   message names the four kintera features behind the floor.
3. *A library or its headers is not found.* Each locator's `REQUIRED_VARS` fails the `REQUIRED` `find_package`.

At import time, `import snapy` fails if `pydisort`, `pyharp` or `kintera` cannot be imported (`python/__init__.py`).

**The excerpt.** The requirements as the top-level `CMakeLists.txt` states them:

```cmake
find_package(Torch REQUIRED)
find_package(Disort REQUIRED)
find_package(Harp REQUIRED)
find_package(Kintera 2.6.3 REQUIRED)
```

The first three lines are the unversioned requirements of item 3 of the refusal list above; the last is the floor
of item 2.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| temperature and pressure | {{< code src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp MoistMixtureImpl::_cons2prim >}} | `compute` | component API |
| mixture heat capacity | {{< code src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp MoistMixtureImpl::specific_heat_cv >}} | `specific_heat_cv` | component API |
| final-stage saturation | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} | `pthermo` | component API |
| redo failure query | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::saturation_failures >}} | `take_saturation_adjustment_failures` | component API |
| driver kinetics | {{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}} | `evolve_implicit` | component API |
| integrator options | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `IntegratorOptionsImpl` | component API |
| integrator construction | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}} | `IntegratorImpl` | component API |

| Python imports | {{< code python/__init__.py >}} | `pydisort` | component API |

: Representative active call sites and dependency edges. {#tbl-appe-calls}

Read the call chain as options, construction, evaluation, then failure handling.
The kintera `take_saturation_adjustment_failures` method returns the accumulated failure count and clears it
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:385-390`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L385-L390)).
snapy calls it in one place, `saturation_failures`, at stage 0 of every step, so that a failure counted before the
step is not charged to it ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::saturation_failures >}};
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). The redo check does not call it. It reads
kintera's count `nfail_` on the device and clears it in the same place, so the count is drained once per step without a
host read (`local_redo_flag_tensor`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). The CMake comment above `find_package(Kintera …)` records four steps of the floor: 2.5.8 for `SpeciesThermo`
`names()`/`mu()`, 2.5.13 for this method, 2.6.2 for the `h2o_bryan` liquid beta that `examples/bryan.yaml`
needs, and 2.6.3 for the same-call rate constants that the kinetics Jacobian of `run_hydro` and
`jupiter_evap_precip_1d` takes. The floor at the pin is the last, 2.6.3 ({{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The frozen outline describes the Disort locator as only supporting Python. The actual `PUBLIC` link list above
corrects that description at the source pin. The compiled `src_files` glob ({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}) excludes the legacy
diagnostics directory and files with trailing underscores. Inspection of its source directories finds no active
Disort radiative-transfer call. Radiation-labelled output metadata is not a solver call.
The external radiative time-step limiter mentioned by the outline is not implemented in the pinned snapy tree;
this appendix does not assign external runner keys or a radiation scheme to snapy.

The missing pyharp/pydisort Python dependency declarations and unspecified CMake version floors leave reproducible
installation and supported compatibility ranges unresolved. The requested kintera pin has been read, not built
with this snapy pin.
:::
